source.title: Identification of post-stroke EEG signal using wavelet and convolutional neural networks
source.authors: E. Djamal; Rizkia Ilham Ramadhan; M. I. Mandasari; Deswara Djajasasmita

record.tranche_reason: Compares Adam and SGD on held-out natural EEG data using a different classification task and measure from the optimizer version’s image and language benchmarks.
record.gate_note: The paper reports optimizer comparisons on natural EEG labels. Its feature comparisons are included as conditions on those optimizer results; it does not test random-label memorization, width, convolutional versus fully connected models, batch size, dropout, generalization measures, or memorized-example removal.
record.test_reason: The study compares Adam and SGD training and held-out performance in a new setting: post-stroke EEG classification with VGG19. Its own results bear on V4's optimizer comparison.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's optimizer paraphrase is accurate: the authors favor SGD's higher accuracy despite Adam's greater early-epoch stability. Their broader conclusion also emphasizes feature configuration, reporting 100% training and 90% non-training accuracy with the full feature set.
record.recipe_differences: Natural EEG classification with wavelet-derived and amplitude features using VGG19; the optimizer comparison uses learning rate 0.01 and 500 epochs. The original version concerns image-classification and language benchmarks.
record.method_sensitivity: The optimizer comparison is reported under three feature configurations: amplitude and Beta included, amplitude absent with Beta included, and both absent. The preferred optimizer depends on whether stability or accuracy is prioritized.

fits_no_version.finding: Adam's early-epoch validation curves are described as more stable than SGD's.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adam can produce less oscillatory early validation performance than SGD in this EEG classification setup.

record.peer_reviewed: Bulletin of Electrical Engineering and Informatics, Vol. 9, No. 5, October 2020
record.problems: The paper gives no uncertainty estimates. The comparison is limited to one EEG task, one stated learning rate, one epoch count, and VGG19; broader optimizer tuning is not reported.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and comparison of held-out performance under natural and random labels.
Width beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Image and language benchmarks; optimizer-specific learning-rate and schedule searches; broader tuning; decoupled weight decay; switching from Adam to SGD; word-level language models.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Comparative effects of adding or removing dropout.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with generalization gaps.
Removing memorized examples versus random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: Remove the record's limits_scope label: extending the comparison to EEG does not itself demonstrate a failure or qualification. Comparator rows repeat the same six optimizer contrasts and are not independent evidence. No uncertainty estimates or repeated-run results are reported. The prose's statement about SGD's higher loss and its insignificance is ambiguous; Table 2 shows slightly higher SGD training loss but substantially lower SGD held-out loss.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance on natural versus random labels.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the role of local connectivity.
Image-classification and language benchmarks; broad optimizer tuning; decoupled weight decay; switching optimizers during training; word-level language models.
Large-batch training and the effect of adapting the training recipe.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relationship to the generalization gap.
Removal of memorized training examples and its effect on test accuracy.

relationships.reason: R1–R12 show SGD accuracy of 90/70/70% versus Adam's 80/60/50%, with lower held-out loss throughout, despite both achieving 100% training accuracy and Adam having lower training loss.
relationships.display_finding: SGD achieved higher held-out accuracy and lower loss across all feature configurations despite equal training accuracy and lower Adam training loss; the third configuration included amplitude and excluded Beta.
